linkedin.title: We decided to stop optimizing our feed for time spent.
linkedin.body:
Most news apps measure success by how long you keep scrolling. It makes sense from a business perspective, but it often leads to algorithms that push outrage or endless doomscrolling just to keep your attention pinned to the screen.

At Headlinne, we made a different choice. Our engineering team built our feed to optimize for relevance and clarity instead of duration. We want you to find what you need to know quickly, understand the context, and then get on with your day.

This meant rebuilding how we rank stories. Instead of looking for what triggers the strongest emotional reaction, our system looks for signal-to-noise ratio. It prioritizes factual updates and diverse perspectives over engagement spikes. It is a slower way to build an app, but it is the only way to build a product that respects your time.

We believe the future of AI in news isn't about keeping you trapped in a feed. It is about being a useful tool that helps you stay informed without the clutter.

story_card.headline: Bird flu reaches Australian mainland mammals
story_card.standfirst: A dead fur seal in South Australia is the first confirmed mammal case on the mainland.

steps.label: What happened
steps.text: A New Zealand fur seal died from H5 bird flu on the Limestone Coast in South Australia.

steps.label: How we got here
steps.text: The animal was found dead at Beachport this Wednesday. It is the first confirmed mainland case.

steps.label: Why it matters
steps.text: This marks a fresh escalation in the virus spread. Mammal infections are a significant development.

steps.label: What to watch
steps.text: Health authorities will likely monitor for further cases as the virus spreads across the region.

story_card.caption:
The H5 bird flu virus has been confirmed in a mammal on the Australian mainland for the first time.

A New Zealand fur seal found dead at Beachport in South Australia tested positive for the virus. This is a concerning development as the virus continues to spread across the region.
